text: Convened means came together for a meeting. Here, the world's top measurement experts met in France.
Fluctuations are small changes up and down. Here, each clock wobbles a tiny bit, so many clocks are combined.
A consensus is an agreement that everyone in a group reaches. Here, the experts must all agree on a new definition.
An atomic clock keeps time by counting the steady jumps of atoms. It is far more exact than a wall clock.
Caesium is a soft, silvery metal. Its atoms jump between two energy states at a very steady speed, so they are used to define the second.
An isotope is one version of an element. Atoms of the same element can have slightly different weights.
An atom can hold more or less energy, like a ball on a low or high step. These levels are its energy states.
Microwave radiation is a kind of invisible wave, the same kind that heats food in a microwave oven.
A cycle is one full repeat of something. Here, it is one full jump back and forth of the atom.
Metrologists are scientists who study measurement and make sure units like the second are exact.
Versailles is a city near Paris, France, famous for its giant royal palace.

t: General Conference on Weights and Measures
forms: General Conference on Weights and Measures
text: This is a meeting of countries that agree on the units used to measure things, like seconds and meters. It happens about every four years.

t: International Bureau of Weights and Measures
forms: International Bureau of Weights and Measures
text: This office near Paris looks after the world's official measurements, including the exact time.
This is the shared set of units most of the world uses, like the meter, kilogram, and second.
To redefine something is to give it a new official meaning. Here, the second would get a new definition.
Standardised means made the same everywhere. A standardised time is one time everyone follows.
To co-ordinate is to help many things work together at the right time. Here, one shared time keeps banks and satellites in step.
A financial transaction is a payment or money transfer, like buying something online. It needs an exact time stamp.
Satellite navigation, like GPS, uses signals from satellites in space to find where you are. It depends on super-exact clocks.
A ruler measures length with marks. If its marks are too far apart, you cannot measure tiny things well.
Like clockwork means smoothly and exactly on time. The writer plays with the word clock.
To untie the second from caesium means to stop depending on caesium for its definition, like undoing a knot.
Optical clocks use light, such as lasers, instead of microwaves. Light waves wiggle much faster, so they tick faster.
Lutetium is a rare silvery metal. Here, its charged atoms power a super-exact experimental clock.
An ion is an atom with an electric charge because it has gained or lost a tiny particle.
A laser is a very narrow, pure beam of light. Here, lasers make the atoms jump.
Nature is a famous science magazine where researchers publish their discoveries.
A tick is one small, regular step of a clock. Faster ticks let a clock measure smaller bits of time.
Regular here means very even and steady, with no change in speed.
Portable means easy to carry and move. A room-sized clock is not portable.
Contenders are the ones competing to win. Here, they are the different clock types competing to be the standard.
Ytterbium is a rare metal. Its atoms are held by lasers in one kind of portable optical clock.
Strontium is a soft metal. Its atoms are used in another kind of optical clock.
Suspended means hanging or held in place. Here, lasers hold the atoms in place.
An uncertainty is how much a measurement might be off. Scientists state it so people know how far to trust a number.
This is a respected physics journal where scientists report new results.
A transition is the jump of an atom from one energy level to another. The new second would be based on one such jump.
Time lords is a joke, like a title from a fantasy story. It means the experts in charge of deciding what time is.

t: Consultative Committee for Time and Frequency
forms: Consultative Committee for Time and Frequency
text: This is the expert group that advises the world's measurement bodies on time and on how fast things tick.
100m means 100 million. A hundred million seconds is about three years, which is the time left until 2030.
